root_cause.text: The function `e1000_tbi_should_accept()` lacks validation of the descriptor-reported `length` before using it as an index (`data[length - 1]`) to read the last byte of the frame, allowing an out-of-bounds access when `length` is zero or exceeds the RX buffer size.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "This happens because the TBI check unconditionally dereferences the last byte without validating the reported length first: `u8 last_byte = *(data + length - 1);`". The patch adds checks `if (unlikely(!length))` and `if (unlikely(length > adapter->rx_buffer_len))` to prevent the OOB access. The KASAN report confirms a slab-out-of-bounds read on a `kmalloc-2k` object.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add bounds checks for length before accessing the last byte of data in e1000_tbi_should_accept to prevent out-of-bounds reads.
intent_record.what: Added two conditional checks before accessing data[length - 1]: one for zero length and one for length exceeding rx_buffer_len. The variable last_byte is now declared separately and assigned after the checks.
intent_record.how: The function now returns false if length is zero or greater than adapter->rx_buffer_len, preventing out-of-bounds memory access when reading the last byte.
